root_cause.text: The HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT flag was set before proto->open() initialized hu->priv, creating a race window where a TTY write wakeup could schedule write work that dereferences the uninitialized hu->priv pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the set_bit(HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT) from hci_uart_set_proto() (before proto->open) to after proto->open() in hci_uart_register_dev(), ensuring hu->priv is initialized before the flag allows work scheduling. The CVE description details the race sequence where CPU1's write work accesses hu->priv while it's still NULL.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT flag to correctly mark the start of protocol initialization and prevent race conditions.
intent_record.what: Added a line to set the HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT flag in the hu->flags bitfield immediately after successful registration and before checking for pending initialization.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures that the HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT flag is set early, indicating that protocol initialization has begun. This can be used by other parts of the driver to synchronize state and avoid duplicate or premature operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature setting of HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT flag to prevent stale flag on registration failure.
intent_record.what: Removed the line `set_bit(HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT, &hu->flags);` from the `hci_uart_set_proto` function, which was setting a flag indicating protocol initialization.
intent_record.how: The flag `HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT` is no longer set during protocol setup, so any code checking this flag will not see it as initialized. This prevents the flag from being left set if the subsequent `hci_uart_register_dev` call fails.
